Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#2023. Sources: Mauricio Pochettino heads to Man United but his first training session delayed

Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. FOCUS Exclusive reporting, domestic and international transfer markets, and elite-level insights. THE INSIGHT Pete utilises a Global Network of Industry Sources to deliver verified, first-to-market reporting. His “Deep-Lens” analysis connects the dots between boardroom strategy and pitch-level recruitment, providing a level of transfer clarity that goes beyond surface-level rumours.

Mauricio Pochettino will take his first training session at Manchester United next Thursday, sources have told Football Insider.

The Red Devils confirmed the appointment of their new manager on 13 November, in a statement which confirmed he join following his duties with the USA national team.

Pochettino will lead the USA one final time in their Nations League quater-final against Haiti on Saturday, before officially joining his new club when he becomes available.

As I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Pochettino is set to arrive back in England next week where he will take charge of his new club.

Man United immediately set their sights on the former Tottenham boss after they were made aware of a release clause in his contract with the USMNT which they were happy to pay.

Following Michael Carrick's dismissal, they have moved quickly to land their next manager, with all parties keen to get working ahead of a tricky run of fixtures coming up.

Football Insider revealed on 11 November that Pochettino had reached an agreement to become the next Man United manager, with backroom staff to join alongside him.

Sources say that the former Tottenham boss join alongside his long-standing assistants Jesus Perez and Miki D'Agostino, as well as goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez.

His first game as Man United manager will be a high-pressure trip to face Liverpool at Anfield, where a defeat could leave them bottom of the table depending on other results.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "He’s still got a couple of games with the US national team at the moment, with this Nations League quater final against Haiti.

"As soon as they're done, I'm sure we'll see Mauricio Pochettino probably arrive in England next week, probably next Thursday when he'll take his first training session.

"That confirmation from Man United was always expected to be announced today or at least over the weekend.

"Obviously then all eyes will be on Pochettino with his first game in charge away at Liverpool next week, as United will be hoping that he is the man that can turn around their fortunes."

Pochettino was quickly identified as the first choice candidate for the Man United job, despite links with the likes of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann in recent weeks.

The former Tottenham boss has plenty of experience coaching in the Premier League and has long been admired by the decision-makers at Old Trafford.

However, former Man United coach Mick Brown warned Football Insider that Pochettino may not be the right man to lead the Red Devils back to their previous success.

While his remarkable work at Tottenham still earns him high praise, the boss struggled to make an impact at Paris Saint-Germain or Chelsea in the following years.

Those spells, alongside his role in the USA's controversial World Cup campaign, have set alarm bells ringing about what might turn out to be another poor Man United decision.

#2022. Dejected Dimitar Berbatov has his head in his hands as he realises Man United are now in relegation zone - but admits old side DESERVE to be there

Published: 18:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 20:33 EST, 7 November 2026

Former Manchester United legend Dimitar Berbatov has blasted his old side, saying they deserve to be in the relegation zone.

United plunged into the bottom three on Saturday afternoon, perversely as neighbours Manchester City lost 3-1 away to Nottingham Forest.

The Bulgarian looked devastated when he was informed of United’s predicament while working on beIN Sports' coverage of the City game but still sounded hopeful that United could turn their form around.

When his attention was drawn to the Premier League table, the two-time Premier League winner initially had his head in his hands before saying: 'I don't believe it, but the way United are playing sometimes they deserve to be there honestly.'

Berbatov then took up a more positive tune saying: ‘Tomorrow they still have a game.'

United host Aston Villa on Sunday and after winning against Roma in midweek have the perfect opportunity finally to end their seven-game winless run in the league.

Berbatov could barely look at the table after United plunged into the drop zone

Berbatov won five major trophies as well as Premier League golden boot in four years at Manhchetser United

The fixture could prove either to be the nail in the coffin for United manager Michael Carrick or afford him more time after a woeful start to the season.

Berbatov won his two Premier Leagues alongside Carrick and will hope his ex-colleague can find a way to keep his job.

If he fails to guide his team to a victory against Villa it could be bleak for Carrick, as he has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa.

Club chiefs handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in ten games.

But now the onus is on Carrick to build on the momentum gained from their Champions League victory.

#2021. Rumoured Liverpool transfer target has been told to find a new club; he left Van Dijk bemused

One player who’s recently been linked with a move to Liverpool has reportedly been told that he’s free to leave his current club.

Two years on from being first linked with Malo Gusto, the Reds are understood to have maintained their interest in the Chelsea full-back and even made enquiries about him during the summer (TEAMtalk).

The same outlet reported that the Blues are seemingly holding out for a world-record fee for a right-back, which is currently held by Achraf Hakimi when he joined Paris Saint-Germain for €68m (then £60m) in June 2021.

According to Si Phillips Talks Chelsea, Xabi Alonso has told the French defender that ‘it is time he finds a new club’, with the ex-Liverpool midfielder preferring to put his trust in Marco Palestra and Josh Acheampong for the long-term.

It’s claimed that there have been ‘no fallouts’ from Gusto apparently being told that he’s surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, with the message being delivered to him ‘respectfully’.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The 23-year-old made a name for himself at Anfield just a couple of weeks ago, but not for the most positive of reasons.

The Chelsea right-back melodramatically threw himself to the ground after mild contact from Virgil van Dijk, who simply looked bemused by the Frenchman’s reaction, and he also petulantly waved his boot at the assistant referee in a futile attempt to get Bradley Barcola yellow-carded.

Those actions certainly didn’t do anything for his popularity among the natives, and it seems indicative that Alonso is apparently prepared to jettison him only a quarter of the way through his first season as Blues manager.

With all due respect to Gusto, Liverpool’s efforts to bolster their right-back options in the medium-term would be better served by trying to secure a permanent transfer for Ronald Araujo, who’s been excelling in that position since joining on loan from Barcelona in August.

It’d definitely make a lot more sense than paying upwards of £60m for the Stamford Bridge defender, especially if Jeremie Frimpong and/or Conor Bradley were to regain form and fitness in the second half of this season.

#2020. Player Ratings: Genoa 1-2 AC Milan – De Winter, Pulisic and Rabiot take charge

AC Milan responded to the criticism with an important win at Genoa on Sunday afternoon. A few players made the difference and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After the mid-week failure against Ferencvaros, Milan knew that three points were more or less a must against Genoa. Thankfully, aside from a dramatic ending, it was a comfortable game for the Rossoneri and a few of the players also got to send some strong signals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

👎 Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

👔 Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

Maignan (6.5): We saw a couple of good stops from him, including one on Vitinha in the second half, and his distribution was decent. He couldn’t really do anything about the goal either, as it was a really good effort from Ellertsson.

Gila (6): I liked his performance overall but there were a couple of moments that dragged down the rating for me, more specifically the fouls he committed. Put simply, he was a bit too rash and it was after one of the free-kicks he caused that Genoa scored their goal.

De Winter (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Diawara (6): He was carded for a very rash challenge, but apart from that, he kept his calm at the back and had decent positioning throughout. It’s not like Genoa threatened Milan a lot, but enough for a pass here still.

Moreira (6.5): It was a lively start from him, I would say, with some good moments on that right flank. However, the end product wasn’t always amazing (some blocked shots), and he faded a bit attacking-wise as the game went on. Solid though and he did put in a defensive shift at the end.

Modric (7): We got to see some really nice flicks and quick play from him today. Defensively, he contributed as well, which was especially clear with a last-ditch toe-poke to avoid a 1v1 for Genoa. There was one poor pass into the middle which could have proved costly, but the rest was good.

Rabiot (7.5): He was back to his usual self today after what was a subpar display against Ferencvaros. Great movement between the lines and elegance on the ball were his main strengths, also getting the assist for the opener.

Musah (6): We have to praise him for doing well in a ‘new’ position, following the instructions from Amorim nearly perfectly. What stopped him from getting a higher rating here was the big giveaway at the end, which Genoa really should have done more with.

Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

Cisse (7): It was a very tidy finish to give Milan the lead, showing once again that he knows how to turn up in the right place at the right time. However, for a higher rating, I would have liked to see more in his 1v1s, which weren’t always so successful.

Ramos (5.5): I’m torn here. It was unselfish to pass to Pulisic for the second goal rather than shooting himself, so that deserves praise. However, I actually think he was very sloppy in open play with heavy touches and positioning that sometimes left a lot to be desired. I suppose the big question is how much his defensive work rate is worth to the rating.

Terracciano (6): Surprisingly good! He had a crucial deflection on a shot from El Shaarawy and also headed the ball away quite a few times in the end, certainly contributing to the three points.

Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

Jashari (6): We didn’t see much in terms of attacking contributions and build-up, since he came on with ten minutes to go, but he was responsible for a few clearances at the end.

Estupinan (5.5): I don’t think it was much of a foul, but in those moments, you shouldn’t even give the referee the opportunity to blow the whistle. He knows that.

Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

This I get a smart striker occasionally does but this guy never does any other runs. This quality of creating space for others to score is one I’ll never get. The same was said about Leao too when nothing else was working for him.

Absolutely! I remember they were saying the same thing for Gimenez too. Literally the same thing..they were saying “he contributes, it is more than just goals” etc. And Ramos pass to Pulisic was terrible. He is lucky Pulisic didnt miss it. It shouldn’t even count as assist.

This is probably the last game to give Camarda an idea on what Amorim’s plans for him are. Up 2-0 he still couldn’t get anytime. He simply wants his $75M friend to score one. Desperate. Camarda should leave for his own good and career.

A few thoughts Positives 1. This was a really good win. We played an inform team in front of a loud crowd and came out swinging. There were some nerves with this one but a 2-1 win is a great result. 2. The Genoa goalie made no good saves. Mike made 3-4. He really is a world class guy 3. Ramos had a hand in both goals…he needs to score, but he was definitely a positive today 4. Cisse shows up in great spots and has a ton of confidence. Am I the only one who thinks he should be a striker? He has a poachers mentality, presses well and has good hold up play. He is not great in the build up or tracking back….so I’d love for him to get a few games up top. 5. Pulisic, Rabiot, and Modric….so smart and always moving into good positions without the ball. It helped keep that lead. Negatives 1. How long do we have to wait for Milan to be a team where most of the players have good vision? Musah, Cisse, Jashari, Hutchison, Moreira, Pavlović no one sees the pitch well. 2. Our depth sucks. As soon as the subs came on, our level of play fell apart. 3. If you are going to allow physical play, the ref cannot call that foul on Estupian. Such garbage

Amorim must know by now that rotating 5-6 players each match will lead to inconsistency and will ultimately get him fired. Today was a win with the right players on the pitch. And the right players in the stands.

From October 11th up until today, November 8th, Milan played 9 games in 28 days. Let that sink in before you try to complain about rotations. Also, outside of Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today. He has no choice but to rotate and use the same players because that’s all he has at his disposal because of injuries and lack of depth.

“Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today.”

So that means he didnt rotate against Ferencvaros? Which is worse because that means he threw that game away by his horrible tactics.

He rotate the starters so they can get some rest. Did you watch the 2 games? What do tactics have to do if the other teams players play harder than Milan players? What does tactics have to do when Milan players pass to the wrong team, or cant make a simple pass forward? When Musah today lost the ball that led to a Genoa chance and Mike saved, was that due tactics or individual mistakes? At the end of the day, the players play on the pitch, not the coach. The coach can have the perfect tactics but if players make individual mistakes or fail to execute the tactics how is that poor tactics?

Important victory ✌️❤️🖤 Now the Germans are coming, so hopefully they will start cleaning the team of trash like El Stupido, Shіtshari, Camarda and always injured parasites like Loftus Merdus Chick, Chukweze and Salamaker!

If we are being honest, Milan’s two goals were ‘freak’ goals. On the first goal, Pulisic won the ball back on his own, then Ramos made a nice decoy run to open up space for Cisse. The second goal was a gift from Genoa. Milan’s offense created nothing the entire game.

Happy Ramos got an assist cuz he was vital to both goals, so often he makes the decoy run to open space for the 2nd runner. With better service he’d score plenty himself, but we dont create many good chances at all. Terra also did much better today, definitely crucial to keeping the 3 points.

I feel bad for Jashari cuz on their goal hes literally the ONLY one trying to close anyone down,everyone else just stands off and let’s him shoot… we really need someone who can create more clear cut chances for the forward line cuz we simply do not create enough clear cut opportunities, so many come down to the other side making an error themselves. Glad we scraped the 2 points out today at least

I hope in the next game Milan don’t rotate heavily….maybe 1 or 2 changes max. Otherwise next game it won’t be consistent again. You just have to stick with same players to gel up.

Milan exaggeration in playing in the back almost lost them the game. I dont understand why its so difficult for Milan in the last decade to build quick attacks. Nonetheless, 3 points earned. I hope the manager can fix these observations and realize the fans like a fierce Milan.

#2019. Steven Gerrard explains his theory on why Alexis Mac Allister has been so resurgent this season

Steven Gerrard has offered a theory as to why Alexis Mac Allister has looked so resurgent this season compared to last.

The midfielder was one of the Reds’ most disappinting players of a dreadful 2025/26 campaign, especially having been such a key component in the preceding Premier League title triumph, but he’s been playing near to his best since Andoni Iraola took charge in the summer.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily (via Liverpool Echo), our former captain claimed that the 27-year-old subconsciously let his performance levels drop last season as he was privately consumed by trying to retain the World Cup with Argentina.

Gerrard said of Mac Allister: “I’ve loved him this season. I think last year, like a lot of the Argentinian players, they had a bit of a distraction with the World Cup coming up.

“It’s the way they are. The World Cup takes over everything in their lives, and I lived that with Emiliano Martínez when I was at Aston Villa. I just think it becomes a priority.

“I think it becomes a bit of a distraction. It becomes the most important thing in their lives, to be ready and not injured and make sure that the national team is the priority.

“I think with a lot of the Argentina players, I’m sure a lot of managers, if they watch this, will say: ‘Yeah, I’ve experienced that.’”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It’s an interesting theory that Gerrard has put forward to explain why Mac Allister’s performances from last season to this have been so chalk and cheese.

Many footballers consider the World Cup as the pinnacle of their careers, and the Liverpool midfielder represents a nation where the sport is nothing short of an obsession.

Only the 27-year-old could truthfully answer whether or not he let his levels dip in 2025/26 because he was prioritising the global tournament in North America, but from a Reds perspective we’d hope that isn’t the case.

As a player employed by LFC, Mac Allister has a duty to give full commitment to representing the club. As disappointing as his performances were last season, though, we wouldn’t go as far as accusing him of not giving less than 100%, which’d be a serious indictment of an elite footballer.

Thankfully, the Argentine has looked much more like his usual self since August, to the point where Troy Deeney suggested that he would even inspire Liverpool to nudge their way into the Premier League title race if he maintains or improves further upon his current standards.

The 27-year-old has been vocal about his contract situation at Anfield, but if he keeps playing the way that he has been, securing a new deal for him should become a matter of priority for sporting director Richard Hughes.

#2016. Kai Havertz's offside problem: Arsenal star has been caught astray FIFTEEN times already this season - and even Mikel Arteta admits striker must address his issue - as imperious defence bails champions out again

Published: 02:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 02:26 EST, 8 November 2026

There’s being eager to break through on goal — and then there is Kai Havertz.

Aside from squandered chances, the sight of the Arsenal striker being caught offside at some point in a match this season is an expectation.

Havertz has been penalised for offside 15 times in the Premier League this season, which is seven times more than Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (in 2nd on eight offsides).

Last season, Bukayo Saka was caught offside 14 times in the league. It is not good enough, and an issue which must be rectified.

A wider scoreline, fronted by Havertz taking his chances, would often change the trajectory of Arsenal matches. Certainly, the 1-0 victory against Hull City on Saturday didn’t need to be so tight.

Mikel Arteta, who can often be defensive of scrutinised players, didn’t even try to mask Havertz’s offside problem afterwards.

Kai Havertz has an issue with repeatedly being caught offside and Mikel Arteta knows he must improve that aspect of his game when leading the line

He said: ‘Yes, it’s something to improve. That's related sometimes to the timing (of the delivery) or really the situation, or the position, where he's lined up and what space he's given. But certainly it's far too many (offsides).

‘I think the sample is quite short to analyse it, but you have a point there. It's a combination. It's all about timing. So there is a signal on the ball, and you need to time it around that.’

A number of deliveries into the final third saw the striker caught out for getting too excited and breaching the backline too early.

The most crucial stray offside against Hull was on the stroke of half-time, Martin Odegaard’s pass aimed in the path of Havertz. As he reached for the ball, Nobel Mendy had grabbed the German’s shirt, tugging him back. A VAR check resulted in referee Farai Hallam announcing that the shirt pull was a foul — but Havertz was offside, meaning no penalty.

It’s a more complex situation, though, than the German simply being too eager in latching onto deliveries.

His team-mates are, on occasion, guilty of not passing to Havertz more sooner. Instead of playing the ball as soon as the opportunity opens up, the delay causes the forward to second-guess himself on when to break ahead.

So the onus is on the Arsenal midfield to time their through balls better, and better understand Havertz’s patterns of play, too. If both elements can click, Havertz and Arsenal’s goal tally will see an uptick.

Otherwise, only the striker’s offside infringement tally will continue to be the beneficiary.

Havertz will latch onto more chances if he is played in at the right time by midfielders

A 1-0 to the Arsenal pattern is already emerging.

Saturday’s victory over Hull was the Gunners’ fifth by such a scoreline across all competitions this season.

The ability to edge matches is a necessary ingredient in a title-winning campaign, particularly in sub-optimal performances.

The Gunners were seriously wasteful in their chances, which better sides will punish. Yet, it’s their ability to carry out wave upon wave of attack, almost expecting the sheer pressure to eventually produce a goal, that is ultimately hard for opponents to resist.

Overall, it’s the north London club’s equal-best start to a league season: 27 points from 10 games, equalling the same tally from their 2022-23 campaign. Their title defence is on the right track — according to the points tallies, anyway.

Arsenal's defence has been integral to their success this season and kept another clean sheet

The Hull City blueprint is a plan other underdog sides should assess when facing Arsenal.

The so-called ‘park the bus’ defensive set-ups are a commonality at the Emirates, owing to the calibre of players both in Arsenal’s starting XI and on their bench.

If a team survives the initial onslaught by the hour mark, Arteta typically turns to the bench and breaks a game open with a change or three.

Here, Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Eberechi Eze all came on before 70 minutes, their fresh legs helping breakdown Hull’s stubborn defence.

Still, the visitors’ high backline is a shrewd set-up which did work to great effect - before Odegaard’s strike.

Arsenal expect inferior sides to sit back, soak up the pressure and mount the odd counter-attack.

By pushing defenders higher up the pitch, it forced Arteta to adapt his carefully laid plans and gave his players a different dimension to navigate, slightly throwing them off track. Manager Sergej Jakirovic deserves his credit.

Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic came up with an excellent strategy that other sides could use

The final word must go to Noni Madueke. He’s received his fair share of scrutiny this season, the winger’s end product an area which is continually brought up.

When in full flow, he is so hard to stop because of his quick feet and directness — which is why more is often expected of Madueke. He is some talent.

Eze, on the bench, was called up by Thomas Tuchel for his latest England squad, with Madueke left out.

On the basis of this, and other recent performances, Madueke has been hard done by.

Though, with Saka sidelined, he can use the next two weeks to ready himself for some huge Arsenal games ahead against Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City and Real Madrid. The opportunity to stake a real claim in Arteta’s side is there for the taking.

#2006. Tragic footballer Jesus de Miguel's devastated club Tenerife vow to financially support his one-year-old daughter until she turns 18 - as fundraiser passes £125,000

Published: 03:12 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 03:12 EST, 8 November 2026

Tenerife have committed to financially supporting the one-year-old baby daughter of Jesus de Miguel following the 30-year-old's tragic death this week.

De Miguel, 30, lost his life following a horror collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono in the latter stages of a second division game on the Spanish island.

The striker's girlfriend, Maria Fernandez, and their daughter, Carla, witnessed the incident from the stands. A post-mortem found De Miguel died from 'accidental chest trauma'. It is described in the preliminary report as a 'cause consistent with the player's death'.

The footballing world came together in Tenerife on Thursday for the 30-year-old's funeral, with De Miguel's team-mates, Spain national team coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez offering support to his devastated family – who said his passing has left an 'impossible void to fill'.

And now Tenerife have confirmed they will support De Miguel's family and Carla following their loss.

Club CEO Antonio Manuel Porro Granados told The Athletic: 'Our plan is to stand by the girl and make sure the entire Tenerife family supports her. We want to be there for her at least until she reaches adulthood.

Tenerife have vowed to support Jesus De Miguel's one-year-old daughter following his death

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel was struck by Jesus Owono during a second division contest and lost his life

'This is a commitment we have made at the initiative of our majority shareholder, Rayco Garcia, and one that we all fully support. It is a commitment that Tenerife, as a club, is making to the family and to their daughter, Carla.

'We will provide the maximum possible support in every respect, beyond what we are legally obliged to provide. We are also exploring other ways of increasing the financial support, so that, at least in material terms, the circumstances do not affect their lives quite so much — although, of course, it is impossible for them not to have an impact.'

Tenerife's commitment follows the development that a fundraiser for the family has passed £125,000 in donations. Spanish footballers Alvaro Morata and Alex Baena are among those who have pledged to the crowdfunding campaign.

De Miguel's family are also reportedly set to receive around £300,000 in base compensation following his death.

Goalkeeper Owono has shut down his Instagram account and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash he has received – which saw him subjected to chants of 'murderer' by the Tenerife fans as he left the pitch.

On Wednesday, he issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Tenerife say they will financially support the family, while a fundraiser has amassed more than £125,000 in donations

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged on Tuesday that homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

#2004. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

Enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

There will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

Clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

Jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

Yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

Understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

Zirkzee’s trickery down the right leaves Justin in his wake but having done the hard bit he fluffs the cross, delivering it too high for a shot and too low for a header. Thompson tries to contort himself to reach it but no one is that flexible.

Couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

Just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

Lammens saves from Harry Wilson’s shot from 10 yards after Rodon’s underlapping ran down the right caught Amass off guard.

Senne Lammens to the rescue! 🧤A great reaction save from the Belgian 👏🇧🇪 pic.twitter.com/GRau9yk02n

Thompson tackles Rodon as he tried to lengthen his stride down the right.

Oddly Bornauw, who is poised to join Hamburg on loan, is the only player kept on from the first half for Leeds.

Gnonto, who is playing at right wing-back, is palyed down the line by Rodon and bends over a low cross looking for Calvert-Lewin’s late run. Lammens dives out to smother it.

Manchester United make three changes – Tynan Thompson, Toby Collyer and Dan Armer replace Santos, Heaven and Dorgu.

Cairns; Rodon, Bornauw, Cresswell; Justin, Ampadu, Stach, Gnonto; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.

Pleasant summer watch between largely second string players. Mbeumo looks a class apart from the other attacking players. On this evidence he might be worth a punt for goals and assists topping 25 this season like they did in 2024-25 for Brentford. Though he may have to take pens off Bruno Fernandes to get there.

The ref blows directly on 45 minutes moments after Nmecha rab out of room to control Tanaka’s cross and booted it out for a Man Utd goal-kick.

Manchester United probe patiently for half a minute around the Leeds area but the pass supposed to play Mbeumo through is picked off by Bijol and he plays it out to James who hares off down the left for 50 yards, cuts in on his right after leaving Yoro in his vapour trail, and whacks a shot over the bar from 22 yards.

Yoro hooks Bogle’s long chip out for a throw-in. This time Leeds take it short and try to engineer a crossing opportunity but go back to Trafford when they can’t find space.

Mbeumo’s on fire tonight as he has been all pre-season, causing Leeds problems whenever he runs at the defence. Now he storms down the centre-right and arcs a shot from 18 yards that beats Trafford’s leap and crashes into the underside of the crossbar. Bornauw hacks it away.

Amass tries to play a one-two with Zirkzee but the crucial middle pass of the three, from Zirkzee, goes astray.

Trafford dives to catch Dorgu’s cross. But he then boots his punt out for a throw-in and Tanaka is penalised for tussling with Dorgu who was thrown the ball and set off on a dribble down the inside-right.

Bikol heads Longstaff’s free-kick from the right over the bar after clever work from Bogle to earn the opportunity. .

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (Aaronson) James robs Tyler Fletcher in the inside-left position and sprints towards the 18-yard line before slipping it inside to Aaronson. The once erratic finisher takes a touch to put Heaven on his heels then slots a right-foot shot crisply into the bottom left corner.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

Tanaka has two long throws in from the right. Dorgu heads the first one out for the second which is flicked on by Bornauw but Man Utd clear the second ball.

Tyler Fletcher takes a trick out of his old man’s book by grabbing James round the waist once the speed merchant had knocked the ball past him. Leeds go backwards from the free-kick as Man Utd’s press hounds them.

Trafford confidently catches the cross from the corner then bowls it out 40 yards to set Aaronson off on a counter. His solo raid down the right is stymied by Amass’s diligent defending.

Mbeumo drives down the gap between Muharemovic and Bijol, tries to find Doegu but Bornauw slides in to intercept but only succeeds in playing it back to Mbeumo who lashes a left-foot shot that Trafford tips round the right post at full stretch.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

There is certainly more urgency about Manchester United’s play. Leeds are living dangerously.

In the couple of minutes after the goal Manchester United almost punish Leeds’ high defensive line again but Muharemovic rides to the rescue. Bijol is a very good box defender but he lacks pace.

United’s start has been bright and confident and the system they playing is flipping between 4-4-2 and 4-2-3-1 and the first thought is always to go forward. The goal they have just scored is indicative of how they have started and it’s a positive for Joshua Zirkzee, who has spent much of his time at Old Trafford under a cloud, to have finished it with aplomb. Whether it will be enough to keep him at Old Trafford for the long run remains to be seen, particularly as interest from Italy persists, but what can’t be doubted is his attitude. He looks sharp.

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 0 (Zirkzee) Leeds, on the attack, lose possession down the middle and Dorgu works it out to Mbeumo who beats Bijol 20 yards inside the Man Utd half. He pokes it through the Leeds captain;s legs and hares off down the wing until he gets to the 18 yard line and from there he bends the perfect pass to Zirkzee who sweeps home a shot into the bottom left with his left foot.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Manchester United build slowly down the right and then Dalot injects some urgency by whipping in a low cross. Zirkzee meets it not so much with a shot but with the timing of his arrival on the ball, deflecting it towards the right of goal powerfully, Trafford gets down well to save.

Leeds cross the free-kick into the box and James’ volley strikes a defender in the midriff and then hits the deck when going for the rebound, bundled over by Yoro. The ref waves play on and Manchester Unted counter with Amad Diallo dribbling down the right until tackled by Chadwick at the price of a corner.

Dorgu is penalised for a scissors-tackle on Bornauw. He did get the ball but only after he had caught he blond defender with his other leg. Carrick leaps up to protest, as does Farke but he is saying that Dorgu has twice slid in wildly.

Leeds defend the corner fairly solidly but Manchester United recover possession 30 yards out and set up Dalot to have a crack with a dipping, swerving effort that Trafford pats down in front of his face and catches after it bounces.

Amad Diallo finds Mbeumo down the right and he tries to head the ball across the box but Muharemovic is well-placed to head it back out but an attempt to nod the ball back to Trafford goes astray and the £45m man can’t stop it going out for a corner.

Leeds free-kick for either a foul by Amass on Aaronson or Dorgu on Bogle. Hard to tell, one was a split-second after the other.

Amass pulls back Bogle after being tackled by the Leeds wing-back and Leeds build up the right from the free-kick, earning themselves a throw-in parallel with the penalty spot. In Ampadu’s absence Tanaka is the trebuchet, hurling in the long throw that Bornauw nods on but Manchester united clear the second ball.

Leeds work the ball back to Taafford from the kick off and he chips it long up the right. Dorgu heads it out for a throw-in. Leeds go backwards again and pass the ball around confidently.

Jaka Bijol captains Leeds, Diogo Dalot leads out Manchester United.

They would be as well delaying the start of the game here the concourses outside this magnificent and historic stadium are packed with crowds taking in the solar eclipse. What a genuinely extraordinary moment! There will be plenty of time later this evening to talk about the football, for now attentions are firmly elsewhere!

🤩 Ready for a first #LUFC start! pic.twitter.com/KU5ica0HcG

And for Senne Lammens, a new shirt number, from 31 to Numero Uno:

Lammens is not the only one. Marcus Rashford wore 39 in his debut season with Man Utd, moved to 19 for the next three then changed to 10 when Zlatan Ibrahimovic left the club. The 10 shirt has been given to Matheus Cunha so now he will wear 14, the number he had at Barcelona in his Liga title-winning season.

If you’re watching in the UK, the match is live on ITV. A friendly! Live on ITV.  That’s Croke Park for you.

Leeds United  Trafford; Bornauw, Bijol, Muharemovic; Bogle, Tanaka, longstaff, Chadwick; Aaronson, James; Nmecha.

Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes on the bench, too soon for Mainoo or Rashford even for the bench.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/QpIL2wc3T9

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#2000. Amorim discusses post-Genoa pride, the Ramos ‘team problem’ and losing being ‘end of the world’

Ruben Amorim wants his AC Milan side to fear losing, while he believes Goncalo Ramos’ lack of goals is a team problem.

Milan got their seventh win in 11 Serie A games on Sunday afternoon as they overcame an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Marassi. Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scored in the first half to put the Rossoneri in command, though Ellertsson’s late strike from range made it a nervy finish.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a result and a response that was needed after the dismal defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday night, and it calms some of the turbulence before the international break. However, the search to become consistently good side is one that will continue in a fortnight.

Amorim spoke to DAZN not long after the final whistle to give his assessments on what was an important win for his side but one that they made hard work of in the end, with his words via MilanNews.

A response was expected after the Europa League, and it arrived. But it’s only the beginning. What positive things do you take away from this?

“I’m proud of my players. The most important thing was to be competitive, I said it before the match. If we approach every game like this, we’re one step closer to winning them all.

“There are times when you manage to play really well, but there are also times when we changed our approach and were strong on second balls and played a different kind of football. And that’s what great teams do: they play differently within the same game. I’m really pleased with my players today.”

“What I can say is that we can win every game, but I can’t guarantee we’ll reach that level of confidence by the end of the season. I don’t feel like we’ve got that kind of consistency yet.

“And I don’t want to say anything more than ‘we can win the next game’. Because that’s the feeling I get when I look at the team. But it depends on many things. If we’d had everyone available, we would definitely have been better in the Europa League, too.

“This run of matches has been tough for us with everything that’s happened. But I can say that if we’re competitive, then we can win every game in the league. Let’s focus on that and take it one day at a time.”

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like you did on Thursday and then turn on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

How is Gonçalo Ramos’ development going? He got an assist today…

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1996. Premier League star's career criminal brother beats Home Office bid to deport him to Africa - as he awaits trial for kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery

Published: 03:45 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 8 November 2026

The street criminal brother of a Premier League star has beaten a Home Office attempt to deport him to Africa - by citing his own human rights.

The gang member and aspiring rapper, now in his twenties, was the subject of a concerted four year attempt by the government to send him to his family's country of origin in West Africa because of his shocking criminal record.

The young man, who has never held down a job, is currently in prison for dangerous driving and carrying a knife - while awaiting yet another court case accused of kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery.

During his teens he had played academy football for several Premier League teams but while his brother went on to make it and is now a multi-millionaire, the man instead got sucked into street crime.

And he has been involved in so much anti-social and criminal behaviour since then that he has even incurred a number of gunshot wounds.

But the wannabe rapper has managed to win a long-running deportation bid by the Home Office to kick him out of Britain as an undesirable - arguing that this wouldn't be fair as all his significant ties are here.

A Premier League footballer - who cannot be named for legal reasons - has seen his career criminal brother living in Britian beat a Home Office attempt to deport him back to West Africa

The Home Office first targeted him for deportation in 2022 after he was sentenced to 20 months in jail having been caught with a sword in his waistband, which in turn meant had breached an existing order about his criminal behaviour.

They lost that attempt to get him out of Britain but appealed - and have now lost that appeal too.

The gang member is 'healthy and capable' according to a judge but has never worked - in stark contrast to his hugely successful brother, a full international footballer who has made countless top flight appearances.

A court heard the foreign national has a 'sustained history of criminal offending involving repeated breaches of Criminal Behaviour Orders, possession of offensive weapons, breaches of licence conditions, recalls to custody, and recent charges. He has a history of offending with knives since the age of 17'.

Totaling his various jail terms together he has spent three of the last eight years prison.

But despite his ongoing recurrent criminality, the Home Office has failed in its latest attempt to deport him after a judge ruled he is 'socially and culturally integrated' into the UK and a return to his home country would leave him 'very much an outsider'.

The immigration tribunal decided he would face 'very significant obstacles to integration' in his home country and prevented the government from deporting him by ruling it would breach his human rights.

That decision came despite it emerging that he has an uncle in the country and grew up with a familiarity of the country, including its culture and food, while his mother maintains links to the country and visited as recently as 2024.

But the judge said the 'significance of these ties should not be exaggerated' because he has never been there.

They said his social and cultural identity 'has been almost entirely formed in the UK and by British culture' - even though he was born overseas and his family come from West Africa. The Home Office is appealing the decision and so the brother could still face deporation.

The knife criminal first arrived in the UK in 2006 after being born in another country where he doesn't have nationality.

He is in a relationship with a British woman with whom he shares a baby.

Their child was born in February but the rapper has only met them twice because he remains incarcerated.

There is no evidence that having a partner or child has reformed his criminal ways, a court heard.

The Home Office argued he is a healthy young adult capable of work who has a familiarity with the culture of his home country and has family ties in the country who could provide guidance and support.

But the judge concluded it would breach his human rights because he has never lived or visited and would be an outsider if returned.
