Fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

The Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

Rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

Chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

That is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

Moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

Colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

Monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#1906. Manchester United face £900m Adidas deal threat amid relegation fears

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 17:14

Manchester United's worsening Premier League campaign could have significant financial consequences, with a relegation clause in their £900m Adidas contract allowing the sportswear manufacturer to halve its annual payments to the club.

Michael Carrick's side have entered the November international break in the relegation zone, sitting 18th with just eight points from their opening 10 league matches.

United have won only once in the Premier League this season and are without a victory in their last eight top-flight fixtures, equalling their longest winless run in the competition's history.

Sunday's extraordinary 4-4 draw with Aston Villa offered some relief after two stoppage-time goals rescued a point at Old Trafford, but the result did little to improve their precarious league position.

Their struggles have brought renewed attention to the commercial implications of a potential drop into the Championship, with the club's latest financial disclosures confirming a provision that could substantially reduce one of their most lucrative revenue streams.

Although relegation remains a hypothetical outcome with much of the season still to play, United's Adidas agreement includes both a payment reduction mechanism and a potential termination clause.

United agreed a 10-year extension to their partnership with Adidas in July 2023, taking their relationship with the German sportswear company through to June 2035.

The extension carries a minimum guarantee of £900m, in addition to the £750m guaranteed under the original agreement, bringing the total contractual guarantee across the extended partnership to £1.65bn, subject to adjustments.

However, the club's annual report for the financial year ending June 30, 2026 confirms that those payments are not entirely protected against a decline in sporting fortunes.

Under the agreement, Adidas has the right to reduce the applicable payments for any year by 50% if United's men's first team are not competing in the Premier League.

Crucially, that would be a reduction in the relevant annual payment, rather than an automatic loss of £900m.

The agreement also gives Adidas the option of terminating its partnership by providing one full season's notice if United are relegated from the Premier League or are otherwise excluded from England's top division.

That provision does not mean a termination would automatically follow relegation, but it would give the manufacturer a contractual route to end the relationship.

United's financial disclosures also confirm a separate penalty for failing to qualify for the Champions League.

From the 2025-26 season onwards, their agreement includes a £10m deduction for each campaign in which the men's team do not participate in Europe's premier club competition.

The club's failure to qualify for the 2025-26 Champions League already triggered one such deduction.

These clauses illustrate how United's commercial income is linked to their performances on the pitch, even under a long-term agreement with one of the world's biggest sportswear brands.

The relegation provision would only become relevant if the club actually dropped out of the Premier League, but their current position has made a previously remote contractual scenario worthy of attention.

United have not played outside England's top flight since the 1974-75 campaign, when they immediately secured promotion from the Second Division.

Their last relegation came in 1974, six years after winning the European Cup under Sir Matt Busby.

They have never been relegated during the Premier League era, which began in 1992, although their 15th-place finish in 2024-25 represented their worst final position since the competition's formation.

The current campaign has produced an even more alarming start.

United's position after 10 matches is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when Ron Atkinson was replaced by Sir Alex Ferguson in November 1986.

Ferguson eventually guided United to an 11th-place finish that season, before overseeing a transformation that delivered 13 Premier League titles.

Carrick now faces a very different challenge, with his side having conceded 19 league goals and secured only one win from their first 10 fixtures.

The latest setback came against Aston Villa, when United recovered from two goals down on two separate occasions before Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time.

Their resilience earned a point, but defensive mistakes continued to undermine the team.

Carrick acknowledged afterwards that United had been making matches unnecessarily difficult through avoidable errors, while insisting that their overall performance deserved more than a draw.

The Red Devils will return from the international break with a trip to Liverpool on November 22, a fixture that presents another difficult test of their attempts to climb away from the bottom three.

For now, there is no suggestion that Adidas has taken action over United's league position. The contractual consequences would depend on their final status at the end of the season.

Nevertheless, the club's financial filings establish precisely what could be at stake should their worst start in four decades eventually result in an unprecedented Premier League relegation.

#1905. Cisse like the greats, Amorim surpasses Allegri: All the key stats from Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan won their seventh Serie A game of the season on Sunday afternoon, beating a Genoa side that entered the game in great form.

The home crowd at the Marassi were fired up going into this one given Genoa had won four of their last five. However, goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes was exactly what Milan needed to take the ascendancy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson did score inside the final few minutes as Genoa mounted a late surge in the hopes of snatching a point, but the Rossoneri held on to win 2-1 and move back into the top four places in the table.

Looking at the general stats makes for interesting reading. Milan dominated the ball with 62% possession, but Genoa had nearly double the Expected Goals (1.14 to 0.61), even though big chances ended up being even at two apiece.

The Rossoblu also had nearly triple the shots (17 to 6) and shots on target (5 to 2), while the Rossoneri did not win a single corner. It suggests that Ruben Amorim’s side simply took their moments and sat back, though maybe Daniele De Rossi can feel a bit hard done by.

📊 The stats from the win against Genoa. pic.twitter.com/wr1E6cohcZ

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 8, 2026

Alphadjo Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8).

In terms of minutes per goal in Serie A, Cisse leads the way with one every 81 minutes. That puts him ahead of the likes of Donyell Malen (one every 82), Lautaro Martinez (one every 88) and Gustavo Varela (one every 91).

After 13 appearances for Milan, Cisse is level with Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and Alberto Gilardino on 8 goals. Pierino Prati (10) and Mario Balotelli (12) are the only players to record more.

Milan are unbeaten in their last 11 Serie A matches against Genoa (W7, D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

The Diavolo have won each of their last five Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against one team do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven).

Milan have won three and drawn three of their first six away games this season. The Rossoneri have pnly avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

#1904. Man Utd sack Michael Carrick and provide update on Mauricio Pochettino arrival

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed their new head coach.

Carrick led training at Carrington this week despite it becoming clear a change was imminent as early as Monday evening.

He arrived at United’s training base at Carrington just before 8am on Thursday morning, leaving less than two-and-a-half hours later having been relieved of his duties.

Behind the scenes, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have sought approval from minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to part ways with Carrick, with a deal for Pochettino, currently serving as the USA men’s head coach, in place.

Carrick has been on the brink at various stages this season with United sat in the relegation zone in 18th place after 10 games, winning just once against newly promoted Ipswich Town.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United opted against making a change during the international break in September and October when Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were the leading contenders for the job.

Carrick gave himself a lifeline as United came from behind to beat Roma in the Champions League at the start of the month. United also fought back twice from 2-1 down in the same game against Aston Villa on Sunday to rescue a 4-4 draw but the decision was made the following day to part ways with the former midfielder.

His staff are also expected to leave, including former defender Jonny Evans who was pictured leaving Carrington with his belongings on Wednesday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carrick’s departure marks the third season in a row United have sacked a manager midway through the campaign.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino’s first game in charge is expected to be the visit to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Carrick, who had a brief spell as interim boss in 2021, took the reins again in January following Ruben Amorim’s dismissal, securing hugely impressive wins over Manchester City and Arsenal in his opening two games.

They won 12 of their 17 games during the second-half of the 2025-26 season, securing third place and Champions League qualification with a game to spare. United picked up more points than champions Arsenal managed in the period from Carrick’s game in charge until the end of the campaign.

United clearly benefited from the lighter schedule in that run with just the Premier League to focus on. With European football back on the menu this season, reinforcements were needed.

United signed three new midfielders in the summer in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba but missed out on their top targets Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes who joined Manchester City and Tottenham respectively.

The club also failed to sign another left-back and a striker – positions they were in desperate need of cover for. United are paying the price now with Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko injured.

Before the comeback victory over Roma, United’s only wins this season came at home to Ipswich and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah. Following a particularly harrowing defeat to Como in the Champions League, club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly challenged the manager’s tactics with the skipper dropped for the subsequent game against Chelsea.

Following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Carrick was applauded off the pitch by supporters who instead turned their ire towards the players in a clear picture of where the frustration lies.

#1903. Star of Mauricio Pochettino’s Spurs side reveals how he will change Man Utd

Former Tottenham star Toby Alderweireld says Mauricio Pochettino is the man to change the mentality at Manchester United and will bring intensity to the team.

Michael Carrick has been dismissed as Red Devils manager, with confirmation coming from the club on Thursday morning.

The club legend’s interim stint from January to the end of last season could scarcely have gone better, but his permanent spell in charge has been disastrous, with United winning just one of their 10 Premier League games this campaign.

Pochettino is now expected to be announced as Carrick’s replacement, with the USA manager set to leave his role and return to the Premier League where he has previously managed Chelsea, Southampton and Spurs.

His stint in charge of Tottenham was the most significant of his career, leading the club to a Champions League and second-place finish in the Premier League.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Alderweireld was a big part of that success, playing for Spurs from 2015-21, and he has high hopes for his former boss at Old Trafford.

‘He will make players fit, that’s for sure,’ the Belgian told talkSPORT. ‘Second of all he brings intensity. It’s not like everyone is playing their own game, he wants a team that’s going to be on the front foot. He wants to play pressure and having the ball as well.

‘A clear idea, intensity and players being fit, I think that’s the way he likes to work.’

Alderweireld reckons Pochettino is going to want the club to bend to his will to some extent, expecting the Argentine to insist on influence in the transfer market.

‘The summer, maybe the winter as well, the transfer window is going to be the players that he wants,’ said the former defender.

‘Then he’ll want to buy the players. Maybe not always the biggest names, biggest talents, but guys with desire to win, desire to become better, desire to run. I think if you see the players he bought for Spurs, that’s thing number one, the desire to become better, the desire to win games, wins duels, to run.

‘That’s why I think Pochettino is the man for Man United, to change things around. In the past couple of transfer windows they’ve bought good players, good quality but they miss some chemistry, they miss the intensity and I think Pochettino will bring that.

‘He brings the mentality. If you work hard and bring your A game every single day, everything you want you can achieve. He will bring intensity and the mindset will change at Man United.’

#1902. South Korean star Kim Min-su has no goals and no assists, but it's no problem for Rangers boss Derek McInnes

Published: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 14:24 EST, 8 November 2026

Kim Min-su’s stat sheet since making the big-money move to Rangers over the summer should be the kind of thing that makes a manager legitimately wonder if both he and the club have been taken for a ride.

Twelve games, zero goals, zero assists. A rank-rotten return, on the face of it. So why does Derek McInnes not seem even remotely concerned by the whole palaver?

Well, simply put, he has a set of eyes. He, like everyone else, can clearly see that the South Korean is the heartbeat of everything that has been good about Rangers in an attacking sense ever since he was thrown into the team – even if the numbers don’t quite back it up.

It was the same story in yesterday’s hard-fought – but deserved – 2-0 win away at St Mirren.

It was hard to keep track of the number of times Min-su drifted in from the left-hand side to pick up possession with no opposition player within five yards. That’s not luck, it’s intelligence.

There is nobody playing in Scotland’s top flight more adept at taking the ball on the turn and driving into space either.

South Korean Kim Min-su contributes to all that is good about Rangers' attacking work

Min-su made life difficult for St Mirren during Rangers' 2-0 victory over the Paisley side

Dan Neil scores Rangers' second in a win that keeps them within four points of leaders Celtic

St Mirren couldn’t get near him for the majority of the first hour. They aren’t the first side to experience such difficulties, and they won’t be the last.

In full flight, he is a joy to watch operating in that pocket between the opposition midfield and defence.

It’s the bit after that where things start to become a little trickier for the talented 20-year-old.

He squandered a couple of opportunities to open his account here. The first came after playing a neat one-two with James Penrice late in the first half, with the ball sitting up perfectly for him ten yards out to smash home.

The choice to take one touch too many allowed Declan John to clear the danger.

So much of his game is based on instinct. Indeed, it’s a big part of what makes him such captivating viewing. But his decision-making in front of goal needs a lot of work.

Perhaps he’s guilty of overthinking things too much.

His manager certainly thinks so, admitting post-match that he felt Min-su was becoming ‘obsessed’ with registering his first goal for the club. In key moments, that shows.

A heavy touch early in the second period after being played in by Badredine Bouanani – unusually quiet here on the right – once again suggested he is feeling the pressure.

But let’s not forget, he’s essentially a kid trying to find his feet in a new country, and in a league which couldn’t be more different in terms of speed and style from what he was used to in Spain.

That he has actually managed to settle in so seamlessly should be applauded. It can’t have been an easy transition but he has quickly endeared himself to the supporters.

It’s why they are every bit as desperate as the player himself to get the monkey off his back.

They needn’t worry. If he keeps doing what he’s doing, the goals will come. Of that there is no doubt.

Some context has to be attached to his failure to notch an assist too. It’s a misleading stat, given that it depends entirely on someone else putting the ball away when it counts.

Min-su created multiple chances for his team-mates in Paisley, the best of which saw Kevin Kelsy put through on goal. It’s hardly his fault that the big man fluffed his lines. The Venezuelan has been in good form but had a stinker here.

At some point, everything will come together for Min-su. And it’s not as if he didn’t have an impact in both of Rangers’ goals against St Mirren.

It may have gone unnoticed amongst everything else, but he absolutely busted a gut to get himself into the box in the build-up to Dan Neil’s deflected strike which sealed the points on 61 minutes. That willingness to put the hard yards in off the ball is every bit as impressive as his ability on it.

And it was his pass to Penrice which led to the full-back being clipped by Samuel Ramos inside the box to give Rangers the opportunity to go ahead from the penalty spot early in the first half.

In truth, they may have been a little fortunate to do so. Put it this way, had referee Nick Walsh not given it, there’s not a chance in hell that VAR would have got involved.

Ryan Naderi stepped up to slot into the bottom corner to take his tally to nine for the season in all competitions.

It says a lot about where Naderi's head is that he had the confidence to do so, especially after blowing a great chance from six yards out only moments before. The German-born Czech international is a changed man, all right.

Speaking of confidence, there is no shortage of it at the other end of the park either. At times, the defensive pairing of Olwethu Makhanya and Emmanuel Fernandez look like they’re playing five-a-sides.

It’s usually the latter who throws in the odd lapse of concentration to add some peril to proceedings, but yesterday it was the normally dependable Makhanya’s turn to give his manager a few hairy moments. Thankfully for the South African, St Mirren couldn’t take advantage.

Craig McLeish’s men could have no complaints over the final result but could have made things interesting late on had either Eseosa Sule or Calvin Ramsay finished from close range.

It’s now just one win in nine for the Buddies, who – much like last season – just can’t seem to put the ball in the back of the net consistently. That problem plagued them so much that they ended up in the relegation play-off spot last year.

McLeish has done an excellent job since taking over from Stephen Robinson. A far better one than anyone could have possibly predicted. He has changed the style of this team completely in a very short space of time and so you have to trust he will be able to find a solution to their goalscoring issues too.

Rangers might be 13 points better off but they head into the international break also in search of that perfect balance.

When they’re on it, they’re very good. But they are still not commanding games from start to finish with any sort of regularity.

They won’t necessarily have to be pleasing on the eye to end up with their hands on the Premiership trophy come May. Celtic’s triumph last season proved that.

The Rangers supporters will gladly put up with imperfect displays for the next six months if that’s going to be the end result.

And if the likes of Min-su can hit the goal trail sometime soon, there’s a decent chance that’s exactly how things will play out.

#1901. Gary Neville tells Mauricio Pochettino to reject Manchester United unless two signings are made

Gary Neville has told Mauricio Pochettino to reject the Manchester United job unless the club promise to sign two defenders in the January transfer window.

Pochettino, who has a $10 million (£7.44m) release clause in his contract with the United States Soccer Federation, has already reached an agreement with United over a move to Old Trafford.

‘I’ve actually asked for Mauricio Pochettino to be the manager of Manchester United probably for seven or eight years and he’s finally going to get it, a bit late in the day for me but he’s finally going to get it,’ Neville said on Stick to Football.

‘He’s going to be sat in the Anfield dugout a week on Sunday, do we think that this is an appointment that will take Manchester United back to a level whereby over three or five years he can keep his job and he can deliver what Klopp did at Liverpool or what Arteta did at Arsenal where there’s that gradual improvement, that feeling you’re on a journey where something can happen?

#1900. Salamanca CF UDS vs Celta Vigo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 17:22, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 17:30

Celta Vigo will aim to avoid a shock elimination in the first round of the Copa del Rey when they tackle fourth-tier outfit Salamanca CF UDS on Friday night.

The visitors have been runners-up in the Copa del Rey on three previous occasions, including in 2000-01, while Salamanca have never been past the second round of the tournament.

Salamanca are managed by a legendary figure in La Liga, with ex-Athletic Bilbao forward Iker Muniain at the helm of the Spanish outfit.

Muniain played 560 matches for Athletic during his professional career, and he is now tasked with helping Salamanca provide a shock in the first round of the 2026-27 Copa del Rey.

Salamanca have been a fourth-tier outfit since 2024-25, earning promotion from the fifth tier in 2023-24, and they are aiming to reach the second round of the Copa del Rey for just the second time in their history, previously securing a spot at that stage in 2024-25.

The hosts will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Real Avila in the league, and they also recorded a 1-0 victory in their last home fixture over Gimnastia Segoviana on November 1.

This fixture had originally been due to take place at the end of October, but it was postponed following the tragic train crash in the province of Toledo, and it was then agreed by both clubs to be played during the international break.

Celta will enter this match off the back of a goalless draw with Levante; the result left them 11th in the La Liga table, picking up 13 points from 12 matches.

The Sky Blues are also playing in the Europa League this season, picking up three points from their four matches in the competition to sit 27th in the overall table.

Claudio Giraldez's side will resume their La Liga action against Real Madrid on November 21 but first have to navigate their way into the second round of the Copa del Rey.

Celta have never won the Copa del Rey, but they have reached the final of the tournament on three previous occasions, lastly finishing as runners-up in 2000-01, suffering a 3-1 defeat to Real Zaragoza in Seville.

The Sky Blues have previously faced Salamanca in the Copa del Rey, recording a 7-0 victory when the two teams locked horns in December 2024.

Salamanca CF UDS form (all competitions):

Salamanca are expected to have Larry Opara at the tip of their attack on Friday, while William Pena is expected to feature in a wide area for the hosts.

Oscar Leon has scored twice in 10 appearances for Salamanca this season, and the 21-year-old is also in line to feature in the starting team.

Salamanca have not reported any injury problems for this match, so head coach Muniain could have a full squad available for the standout Copa del Rey fixture.

Celta have been boosted by the news that Ilaix Moriba has withdrawn from the Guinea squad and will therefore be available for the clash with Salamanca.

However, Sebastian Caceres is unavailable due to international commitments with Uruguay.

Celta will also be missing Borja Iglesias, Carl Starfelt, Jones El Abdellaoui, Alvaro Nunez and Miguel Roman for the cup fixture due to injury problems.

Ayala; Ucin, Murua, Levrand, Rivas; Cristeto, Alsua; Leon, Txoperena, Pena; Opara

Radu; Rodriguez, Lago, Alonso; Rueda, Febas, Burcio, Carreira; Alvarez, Duran, Swedberg

#1899. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1898. Mauricio Pochettino will ditch four Man Utd stars – the winners and losers under new boss

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to take the reins at Manchester United in the club’s latest attempt to reset the clock.

Having been regarded as a genuine candidate for the job at Old Trafford on three occasions in the past, the Argentine now gets his chance in Manchester where United’s situation is more dire than ever.

With Michael Carrick’s exit confirmed, Pochettino will inherit a squad that has been routinely booed off the pitch by a fanbase thoroughly disenchanted with a lack of effort on it. While there may be hopes of recruitment in the January transfer window, Pochettino will have to work with what he has at his disposal until then.

Metro looks across the United squad to identify whose prospects look brighter than ever with the new manager en route – and those who face the axe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

With Benjamin Sesko starting just two matches this season before injury struck again, Bryan Mbeumo has spent most of the campaign operating up top. He could remain in that role until Sesko is fit again but both he and Matheus Cunha stand to benefit in their natural positions under the new regime.

Pochettino has favoured inverted wingers to help create overloads in the middle with Cunha in particular tailor made for that role.

Moussa Dembele evolved into one of the Premier League’s most dominant midfielders at Tottenham under Pochettino, carrying on the work started by Martin Jol at Fulham with the Belgian. Kobbie Mainoo lacks Dembele’s outstanding athleticism but his press resistance and running power with the ball will be regarded as key assets for Pochettino.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mainoo does not have the constant high-energy output Pochettino has traditionally demanded of his midfielders but he has improved his engine over the last two years and his ability to break the lines could also see him play a key role.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all lauded the qualities of Mason Mount despite injuries ensuring they never saw the best of him. Pochettino could be another to look favourably upon him if he can prove his fitness.

When in negotiations with Chelsea back in 2023, Pochettino was eager for the club to end a contract stand-off with the midfielder and was desperate to keep him and make him a key component of his rebuild west London. His own arrival came too late to revive negotiations however with Mount joining United that summer.

Mount’s work rate has never been in doubt and his abilities to run off the ball or intelligently drop into space could be vital. But with just one start in the Premier League this season, the same old doubts are in place.

In October, former United captain Gary Neville called time on the Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, neither dynamic or athletic enough to last the course in the Premier League. There may only be one winner with the Belgian perhaps most at risk.

Tielemans is adept in keeping possession and progressing play but his lack of drive up the pitch is seemingly at odds with how Pochettino likes to set up his midfield. Pochettino was also said to have turned down the chance to sign the midfielder on at least one occasion after his name was put forward by the Tottenham board.

The same concerns for Tielemans could also apply for another summer recruit in Andrey Santos who looks to be another passive operator based on evidence to date.

The emphasis Pochettino puts on his full-backs has been huge during his time in the Premier League but it is the area of the pitch where United are perhaps at their weakest. Diogo Dalot’s shortcomings on the right continue to be exposed while a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw is well overdue.

Dalot’s prospects are brighter – while his final ball is consistently short of the required standard, his ability to get up and down the pitch will be important. Shaw can no longer offer that kind of service on the left and Pochettino may favour the energy of Patrick Dorgu.

Pochettino helped nurture Shaw at Southampton before his £27million move to Manchester in 2014 but the 31-year-old will now struggle to provide the intensity the role demands.

United’s defence has been an utter mess and with the exception of perhaps Leny Yoro, all should consider their futures uncertain. But at 34, Maguire is perhaps the most at risk.

Pochettino favours a high defensive line, requiring centre-halves with pace to live with it. Maguire will turn 34 in March and has been at the heart of a backline that has conceded 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Pochettino may favour the younger legs of Yoro and Ayden Heaven while Lisandro Martinez’s ability to build from the back could keep him in the picture for now.

#1897. Sky: Ramos involved but has minimal support – the numbers that illustrate Amorim’s point

Some interesting analysis on AC Milan and Goncalo Ramos’ attacking struggles has been provided by the Sky studios.

It was a familiar tale for Ramos during Milan’s 2-1 win over Genoa on Sunday. He was involved but rarely inside the box, then he was selfless instead of ruthless in front of goal when he chose to square for Christian Pulisic to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The worries are starting to grow regarding whether the Portuguese can provide the output required of a number nine that cost €70m. Yet, the Rossoneri have scored 23 goals in 11 league games which suggests goals are coming from elsewhere, sometimes with Ramos’ help.

Sky offered some interesting insight after Sunday’s game. Firstly, they picked out just how involved Ramos actually is with various aspects of Milan’s overall play.

For example, he is first among Serie A strikers for interceptions and recoveries, while he is second for receptions, touches and duels. He is third for passes.

He is first among centre-forwards in the league for touches in the middle third of the field and touches in the opposition half. He is second for fouls committed plus fouls suffered among forwards, with 41.

Sky then shift the focus to the team’s overall play to try and explain why Ramos perhaps isn’t getting the quality service and is having to drop deeper as a result.

They look at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of.

What does this tell us? Well, Amorim’s post match assessment about struggling to get the ball from the defensive third into the final third are true. Milan have a lot of the ball but still struggle to progress it, as the coach told Sky.

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals,” he said.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1896. Chelsea injury news: Blues handed Josh Acheampong blow

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 17:38

Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong has allegedly withdrawn from international duty with England Under-21s.

Having been largely snubbed by the likes of Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior, the 20-year-old has starred under Xabi Alonso.

In sharp contrast to 2025-26, Acheampong has accumulated the sixth most minutes of Chelsea's outfield players in this season's Premier League.

However, the academy graduate was a notable absentee from the squad that suffered a 1-0 defeat at Sunderland last weekend.

At the time, the injury being carried by the versatile defender was described as 'minor'.

According to football.london journalist Bobby Vincent, Acheampong has now withdrawn from representing England Under-21s over the November international break.

When Acheampong remained in the group at the start of the week, the assumption had been that he would be available for the games against Portugal and France.

Instead, the youngster has seemingly returned to Chelsea, where he will be assessed ahead of the resumption of Premier League action later in the month.

The report emphasises that Acheampong's fitness issue is not expected to keep him out in the long term.

Presumably, playing him in two international friendlies has not been deemed worth the risk.

He has already racked up nine starts and two substitute outings for Chelsea this season, as well as made two starts for England Under-21s.

Therefore, a brief rest before the resumption of action may prove to be a blessing in disguise for a player who barely played between January and June.

#1895. Alan Shearer hails Arsenal star as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League

Alan Shearer has hailed Arsenal summer signing Ezri Konsa as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League.

Konsa completed a £55m move to Arsenal over the summer after ending his seven-year spell at Aston Villa.

The England defender won the Europa League at Villa Park but has bigger ambitions with reigning Premier League champions and Champions League finalists Arsenal.

Konsa has missed just one game for Arsenal so far this season, helping Mikel Arteta’s side open up a five-point gap at the top of the Premier League and enjoy an impressive start to their European campaign.

The 29-year-old was signed partly due to the absence of William Saliba, who returned from last summer’s World Cup with a serious back injury.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Konsa’s form has led several pundits to question whether Saliba, widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the world, will even get straight back into the Arsenal team.

‘I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa,’ Premier League record goalscorer and former England striker Shearer told Betfair.

‘I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven’t even really mentioned them missing William Saliba.

‘The only time we’ve mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that’s because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good.’

Arsenal’s first game back following the international break is a potentially tricky trip to St James’ Park to face Newcastle United.

#1891. Arsenal transfer news: Viktor Gyokeres makes Mikel Arteta feelings clear amid Gunners exit talk

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 17:39

Viktor Gyokeres has suggested that he has no desire to push for a transfer away from Arsenal.

Having netted 14 goals in the Gunners' Premier League title success in 2025-26, the Sweden international has etched his name in the club's history books.

However, Gyokeres has accumulated just 181 minutes of top-flight football this campaign, with Mikel Arteta showing preference to Kai Havertz.

Although the 28-year-old has featured regularly in the Champions League, being viewed as second choice by Arteta has thrown up question marks over his future.

Nevertheless, in an interview with Fotbollskanalen, Gyokeres has made his feelings clear over recent speculation.

When quizzed on whether he wanted to stay at the Emirates Stadium, Gyokeres replied: "I want to".

Meanwhile, he was naturally asked about his relationship with Arteta, with the Spaniard not always getting the best out of the frontman.

He said: "Communication with Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play.

"Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opposition and what I should be thinking about."

While Gyokeres has perhaps not met people's expectations since his move from Sporting Lisbon, that is not to say that he has not been an asset to Arsenal.

A return of 23 goals and six assists from 69 appearances is an acceptable return, particularly when Arsenal have spent much of that period at the top of the Premier League.

Gyokeres brings qualities to Arsenal that Havertz does not, and vice versa. That is realistically why Arteta appreciates having their different profiles at his disposal.

With Gyokeres having a contract at Arsenal until 2030, there is little prospect of an exit anytime soon.

Morgan Rogers issued a stern defence of Cole Palmer’s committment to the England squad and urged Thomas Tuchel to recall his Chelsea teammate to the national side.

Rogers was on the scoresheet on Thursday evening as England booked their spot in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 win over Croatia.

The 24-year-old is the only Chelsea player in England’s squad for this international break, with Reece James injured and Palmer not selected by Tuchel after he pulled out of the previous camp due to injury concerns.

Speaking last week, the German suggested that Palmer ‘misses too many opportunities’ to play for his country but has insisted that his latest exclusion was ‘not personal’.

Rogers, though, would like to see his close friend back in the national team set-up and said accusiations that Palmer does not want to play for his country were a ‘lie’.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘He wants to be here,’ Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live. ‘He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

‘We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he’s been managing them injuries ever since.

‘He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn’t feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn’t?

‘But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10/15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

‘It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It’s a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England.

‘You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don’t get it and he doesn’t get it. But it’s something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.’

Asked if he thinks Palmer should be back in the England set-up for the next camp, Rogers continued: ‘Of course I do. What a player he is. What a person he is and it’s someone you want to see in an England shirt.

‘He’s got so much quality, so much ability. We all know what we can do, what he’s done, so of course we want to see him in an England shirt and hopefully sooner rather than later.’

When asked about Rogers’ comments in his post-match press conference, Tuchel said: ‘It’s totally fine. It’s his teammate and his friend so why wouldn’t he make an emotional statement?

‘If he did it, I didn’t hear it so I will not comment on it. All I can say is I was very happy with the emotional and physical commitment of Morgan Rogers – I think he was a standout player today, offensively and defensively and that’s what matters.’

#1887. Tunisia vs Libya - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 11 Nov 2026 17:50, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 17:52

Tunisia and Libya will both look to kickstart their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaigns with a win when they meet at Stade Taieb Mehiri on Friday.

Both teams are winless from the opening two matchdays, and a defeat for either side could leave them with too much ground to make up at the midway point of the qualifiers.

After qualifying for each of the last 17 AFCON finals - the longest active streak of any nation - Tunisia have arguably been the most underwhelming team of the qualifiers so far, having been held to draws by Uganda and Botswana.

This continues what has been a torrid 2026 for Moin Chaabani’s men, who are now winless in eight matches and have conceded in each of their last seven outings.

A return of just two points from a possible six leaves the Eagles of Carthage, who have topped their qualifying group five times in the last six editions, third in Group H and currently on course to miss out on African football’s showpiece event for the first time since 1992.

However, much could still change for Tunisia over the course of their double-header against Libya, with the sides set to meet again in Tripoli next Thursday after this weekend’s clash.

Having won each of the last four meetings - all in AFCON qualifying - Friday’s hosts will be confident of overcoming their North African rivals in both upcoming encounters and putting themselves in pole position to clinch an AFCON spot.

While Tunisia have been AFCON regulars, Libya have featured at just three tournaments in their history. Their quest for a fourth began on a positive note, coming from two goals down to earn a point against Botswana in their opening qualifier.

Carrying that momentum into their second outing, Youssouph Dabo’s side travelled to Hoima to face Uganda, where they were arguably the better team but left empty-handed after Arnold Vula’s strike on the stroke of half-time.

Since a five-match unbeaten run (W3, D2) between September 4 and November 15 last year, the Mediterranean Knights are now winless in their subsequent five games, with Dabo’s appointment to replace Aliou Cisse yet to deliver the desired impact.

Libya have managed just one victory in their last 13 AFCON qualifiers and now require two wins in quick succession to lift themselves off the bottom of Group H before the final round of matches in March 2027.

Both of Friday’s opponents have struggled defensively, so goals at both ends look likely. Striking first could prove crucial for the visitors, with the hosts having conceded the opening goal in six of their last seven matches.

Tunisia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Libya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Elias Achouri, Ellyes Skhiri, and Hannibal Mejbri are all ruled out through injury and will play no part for Tunisia on Friday.

Hazem Mastouri’s brace against Botswana means he has now scored three goals in his last two international appearances, so he is one to watch.

Midfielder Ferjan Sassi is one appearance away from equalling Radhi Jaidi’s all-time record of 105 for Tunisia and could make history on Friday.

Ezzeddine Al Mariami has been directly involved in each of Libya’s last three goals, making him the visitors' biggest attacking threat at the moment.

Twenty-five-year-old Osama Al Shreimy plays his club football in Tunisia with Club Africain and will be eager to impress against his adopted home nation.

Dahmen; Nasraoui, Arous, Talbi; Ltaief, Sassi, Laidouni, Maaloul; Gharbi, Ben Slimane; Mastouri

Al Tihar; Jaddour, Al Suwaee, Youssef, Salama; Al Hbeishi, Al Shalui; Elhouni, Al Gsheim, Issa; Al Mariami

Tunisia may be enduring their roughest patch in decades, but they still possess enough quality to overcome an equally struggling Libya side.

We are backing the hosts to make home advantage count and secure all three points after 90 minutes.

#1885. Mauricio Pochettino identifies seven Man Utd stars he is desperate to work with

Mauricio Pochettino is relishing the opportunity to work with a number of Manchester United stars when he arrives at Old Trafford.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has agreed a two-and-a-half year deal to replace Michael Carrick in Manchester with his first game in charge set to be away to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Marcus Rashford could be one of the big winners of the club’s latest appointment with The Daily Telegraph reporting Pochettino has ‘always loved’ the England international.

‘Mauricio has always loved Rashford,’ one source told the newspaper. ‘He will put an arm around him and give him that same kind of love he showed to Dele Alli [at Spurs]. Then it’s up to Rashford.’

Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and was expected to make the move permanent until the Spanish champions backed out of their option to buy. The 29-year-old also spent the second-half of the 2024-25 season on loan at Aston Villa having been frozen out of the team by Ruben Amorim.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

After United failed to find a buyer for him in the summer transfer window, Rashford was reintegrated back into the squad by Carrick in pre-season.

He has started five matches in all competitions this season but a hip injury has ruled him out of the last five.

Rashford hopes to be available for the trip to Liverpool after the international break.

Pochettino will also be reunited with Luke Shaw, who he nurtured as an emerging teenage talent at Southampton before joining United for £27million in 2014.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Shaw is among six other players Pochettino is specifically looking forward to working with alongside Kobbie Mainoo, Patrick Dorgu, Carlos Baleba, Amad Diallo and Bruno Fernandes.

Fernandes has rejected United’s latest new contract offer, casting doubt on his future after the captain publicly criticised Carrick following the Champions League defeat to Como in October.

Pochettino was eager to sign Fernandes back in 2019 when he was still in charge of Tottenham. Spurs were unable to strike a deal with Sporting with the Portugal international joining United six months later.
