Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

#1862. Bulgaria vs Iceland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 20:37

Iceland could clinch promotion to Nations League C by beating hosts Bulgaria on Friday at Stadion Hristo Botev.

The Icelandic national team are currently top of Group C with eight points from four matchdays, whereas their opponents are third with four points and must win if they are to make certain that they remain in the race for promotion.

Given six games will take place in the group, Bulgaria would be unable to catch Iceland if they were to take just a point on Friday, but a win for second-placed Estonia against Luxembourg on the same day would increase their points tally to nine and make them unreachable.

Unfortunately for boss Atanas Ribarski, his side have only won one of their last six games in all competitions, losing on three occasions.

The hosts did beat Luxembourg 2-0 on October 6 in their most recent Nations League outing, and that was their second clean sheet in the group stage.

At the other end of the pitch, the Lions have only scored three goals in this iteration of the competition, and they have failed to find the back of the net in eight of their 15 most recent games.

Bulgaria have lost five of their past 10 clashes at home, a stretch in which they triumphed just once and were held to four stalemates.

Only first place will guarantee progression into Nations League B, and Iceland would secure first if they beat Bulgaria and Estonia lost against Luxembourg.

Head coach Arnar Gunnlaugsson will be frustrated that his side failed to beat Estonia on October 6, when the two sides drew 0-0.

However, Strakarnir Okkar are unbeaten in four games, winning twice, though it may be a concern that they have only won two of their past 10 clashes.

The visitors managed to beat their hosts 3-0 when they met on October 3, winning for the first time in any of their five encounters, with Bulgaria claiming victory three times.

Iceland come into Friday's match having drawn one and won one of their two away fixtures in the Nations League so far, but they were winless in their prior six contests on the road, suffering four defeats.

Bulgaria must be careful to avoid needless yellow cards on Friday given eight players are at risk of picking up a suspension, though they know they will be able to welcome back goalkeeper Dimitar Mitov and winger Lukas Petkov.

Mitov is likely to be stationed behind a back four featuring centre-backs Stefan Velkov and Emil Tsenov, while Andrian Kraev and Ilia Gruev could start in a double pivot.

Petkov is set to start on the right side of attack, with Kristiyan Balov on the left flank and Atanas Iliev through the middle.

Iceland could position Andri Gudjohnsen in an advanced role behind striker Orri Oskarsson, with the pair likely to be supported by midfielders Gylfi Sigurdsson and Isak Bergmann Johannesson.

Central defenders Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Hordur Magnusson are candidates to start in the heart of a back four.

Mitov; Stoyanov, Velkov, Tsenov, Petrov; Kraev, Gruev; Petkov, Rusev, Balov; Iliev

Though home advantage has often been crucial for many teams, Bulgaria have struggled for consistency when playing as hosts.

Iceland have also performed well on their travels in the Nations League, and they should be confident that they can take three points on Friday.

A £60million summer signing from Freiburg, Manzambi has returned to Aston Villa for further assessments on a calf issue.

#1860. GdS: Week-long breaks and lighter sessions – Amorim bringing ‘international culture’ to Milanello

Ruben Amorim’s decisions when it comes to training have once again come under the microscope after the win over Genoa.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that Amorim’s closing message to the players after the victory at the Marassi was music to their ears: ‘See you next Monday’. Until early next week, Milanello will remain closed, leaving the players free to recover from the early season grind.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Who knows if things might have been different had the trip to Genoa had gone differently, but the victory that put Milan back in the Champions League spot is worth the reward of a full seven days off. in the eyes of the coach.

An oddity: Serie A teams usually have a break during the international break, but not this long. It’s also worth noting that Milan’s 13 internationals are currently busy traveling around Europe and the world, while the injured players will also continue to follow their respective recovery programs.

As a reminder, Amorim gave those who were not called up by their national teams eight days off for the last international break. However, if must be remembered that it was an extended three-week one, so there was more runway before games resumed.

The extended break is not the first change introduced by Amorim and his staff. For example, the Tuesday rest granted to the team on the eve of the European trip to Bournemouth. The Rossoneri returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they left for England.

This is an unusual approach compared to the traditional post-match rest schedule or a maximum of three or four days of rest during league breaks. Amorim’s training methods are also new, exemplifying the ‘international culture’ the coach seeks to instil at Milanello.

On the pitch, the sessions are never too hard or tiring. The Portuguese coach himself explained the thinking behind it, emphasising that among the many matches scheduled, the tactics and movements were essentially practiced in-game due to the limited time available between matches.

The concept of over-working players in training amidst a demanding fixture list was thought to be the cause of the many Milan injuries suffered during similar periods. Amorim has sought to rectify it, but then the list of absences for the Genoa game was long, so it all remains a work in progress.

#1859. Celtic 1 Kilmarnock 0: Liam Scales scores only goal as Premiership leaders make hard work of it

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026

For Martin O’Neill, the second international break of the season should be somewhat less fretful than the first.

Seven weeks ago, with a home defeat to Ferencvaros coming in between two no-shows against Rangers, the veteran wondered aloud if it might be time to ‘wrap it up’.

O’Neill later admitted that he regretted his choice of words. He won’t, though, lament the decision to go again as he rests up in the coming days.

While the intervening weeks have often been a bumpy ride, the past four days have been a lot more like it.

Thursday’s dramatic win over Besiktas has breathed new life into Celtic’s Europa League campaign.

While by no means spectacular, this narrow victory over Kilmarnock re-established their four-point lead at the top of the Premiership and will have further dampened the sense of hysteria which was threatening to engulf the entire club.

Celtic defender Liam Scales loops the ball over Kilmarnock's goalkeeper and into the net

Scales celebrates with Camilo Duran after netting the only goal of the game at Celtic Park

Celtic striker Kasper Hogh finds the net with a crisp right-foot shot, only to have it disallowed

Celtic certainly made hard work of this. Truth be told, they should have gone into the break on the back of a far more convincing victory.

While they were right to feel wronged that Kasper Hogh saw his goalless run stretch to 16 matches after having one harshly disallowed, O’Neill’s men did not help themselves either.

Coming after Liam Scales had given them a half-time advantage, Benjamin Nygren’s missed penalty allowed Kilmarnock to keep believing right to the end.

Nonetheless, it was hard to begrudge Celtic their victory over the piece. A few weeks back, this might have been a contest in which they’d have come a cropper. They look more assured defensively than earlier in the season.

You don’t need to stay up all night researching exactly why Kilmarnock are in such peril at this stage of the season.

Neil McCann’s side began the campaign losing goals and they’ve really never stopped. They cough up more chances than any side in the top division. When it comes to shooting themselves in the foot, they’re in a league of their own.

In 13 games to date, they’ve shipped 29 goals and have kept just two clean sheets in the process. St Mirren, the side with the second worst record in the Premiership, have lost 22.

As worrying as those statistics and the Premiership table undoubtedly are, though, this felt like a step in the right direction.

In being more resolute, McCann’s men stayed in the contest right until the final whistle. They fashioned a number of decent chances throughout. There was plenty of encouragement here, even though they went down again.

For the home supporters, the much-needed positivity which had emanated from Thursday’s European win was boosted by the return to the starting line-up of Jota for the first time since April 2025.

Notably, only three out of nine of Celtic’s summer signings made the squad, with Sam Johnstone the only one involved who arrived on deadline day.

O’Neill was indebted to the on-loan Wolves man inside the first minute. Ieuan Owen skipped away from Callum McGregor then Colby Donovan down the left and put in a dangerous cross. Twice Tom Lowery hit the target. Twice the Celtic keeper stood up tall.

Lowery immediately had his name taken by John Beaton for a clumsy foul on Nygren.

Despite their precarious position, to their credit, Kilmarnock didn’t come to Parkhead just to defend. Tyreece John-Jules, their main striker, had an abundance of support in the form of Owen, Greg Kiltie and Joe Hugill.

Between them, they fashioned enough half chances. They just didn’t have ice in the veins at the right moments.

Hogh was right to feel aggrieved at the decision which cost him that elusive goal. Truthfully, there was very little in Mika Baur’s challenge on Kiltie which was retrospectively penalised.

Duran gathered and fed Nygren. The Swede swivelled and rolled the ball into Hogh’s path. A crisp right-foot finish was not that of a player lacking in confidence.

The Dane’s lengthy celebrations included a look up to the heavens. By the time Beaton made his way to the monitor and chalked the goal off, Hogh could have been forgiven for feeling that someone up there had it in for him.

To Hogh’s credit, he didn’t let it affect him. Moments later, after being played in by Duran, he was only denied his revenge by the outstretched leg of Nico Mantl.

Hogh then played Duran in with a clever back-heel. The Colombian lashed his effort just wide.

Celtic’s pressure was mounting and they edged in front on 26 minutes with Duran, yet again excellent throughout, the architect.

His clipped cross from the right caught the Kilmarnock defence flat-footed. Scales extended his left foot and watched the ball rise to the point where it appeared to be going over.

With Mantl hoping that it would clear his bar, it looped into the net. There was no disputing this one.

Required to take more risks, Killie had to be careful when they turned the ball over. Hugill and Cathal McCarthy were both booked for crude fouls on Duran and Jota, respectively.

While Celtic began to control the affair, the visitors were not without their moments. Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s stinging strike from 25 yards forced Johnstone into another solid stop.

While Jota looked good in moments, it’s clearly going to take some time before he’s fully up to speed. The same might apply to Hyun-jun Yang, the man who replaced him at the interval, after being sidelined for six weeks with a hamstring injury.

Donovan came close to wrapping up the three points with an enterprising run and shot with his left foot which flew just wide.

Duran’s close control and speed across the ground bought him a yard for a shot. Having seen it late, Mantl dealt with it well.

Hogh actually performed well here. He was tidy with the ball and frequently brought team-mates into play. He just didn’t hit the target often enough. That again cost him when he spun neatly in the box and tried his luck midway through the second period.

You couldn’t fault him when he seized on Kieran Tierney’s cross, though. The saving block from Killie substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara was tremendous.

With the home supporters longing for a clinching second goal, Duran dumped a shot into the side netting before the industrious Baur was flagged offside after firing home.

The wait would go on. Initially adjudged to have struck Aaron Tshibola’s arm just outside the box, Yang’s strike would earn Celtic a spot-kick with 14 minutes remaining after a VAR review.

Nygren just never looked confident as he spotted the ball. Mantl dived to his right and made a comfortable save. Those hoping for a sharp exit sat back in their seats.

The sight of Baur hobbling badly after being caught by Tshibola didn’t make the viewing in the final moments any easier. All that truly counted for the home fans, though, was that Celtic got over the line.

#1858. Harry Kane becomes England’s most-capped men’s player with 126th appearance

Harry Kane has broken the all-time record for the most appearances by an England men’s player.

By leading his country out against Croatia on Thursday evening, alongside his four children, the England captain overtook Peter Shilton’s long-standing record to move top of the all-time caps list with his 126th appearance.

Shilton was involved in a commemorative tribute to Kane before kick-off in the Nations League game at Wembley, before Prince William presented him with a signed ‘126’ shirt.

The 33-year-old’s tribute before the match also included him parading his Ballon d’Or trophy in front of the Wembley crowd. It is the first time the award for best player has been on English soil since Kane was crowned its winner at the London Palladium 17 days ago.

Kane is already the top scorer in the history of the national team, having netted 91 goals in 125 caps before taking the field against Croatia on Thursday evening.

The skipper has said he wants to “set a challenge” for future England players to beat his caps record.

Midfielders Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice boast 60 and 80 caps at the ages of 23 and 27, respectively, and Kane said on Wednesday: “Look at how young they are, I will try and give them a good number to catch.”

Billy Wright and Bobby Moore shared the record for the most England caps as captain for decades, having each led the Three Lions out 90 times. But having overtaken that record earlier this year, Kane is now on cap 98 as skipper, and is expected to reach a century next year.

The final of four matches during the last international break saw England defeat Czechia 3-0 with two goals from Kane and the other, an own goal, having been set up by the captain.

After the match, Bellingham said of Kane: “He is the best England player to ever wear the shirt and it is an honour to play with him.” England head coach Thomas Tuchel recently admitted he had “run out of superlatives” with which to describe Kane.

#1857. Mali vs Rwanda - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 11 Nov 2026 23:07, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 18:01

Mali host Rwanda at the Stade du 26 Mars in Bamako on Friday, November 13, in the third round of Group K in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with kickoff at 19:00 GMT.

Both sides won their opening two games and sit on six points with a goal difference of +3, Rwanda ahead on goals scored (five to four), and only the top two in a group with no host nation reach the finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Anthony Da Silva's first competitive game in charge of Les Aigles ended in a 3-1 home win over Cape Verde, a side who played at this summer's World Cup, on September 25.

Ange Martial Tia scored after five minutes, Sidny Cabral equalised in the 10th minute, and Nene Dorgeles then scored in the 39th and 51st minutes.

Tia also scored the only goal in Paynesville on September 29, in the 79th minute, after which Da Silva said Liberia had defended well on a synthetic pitch.

A 1-1 friendly draw with Morocco in Tangier on October 4, in which Gaoussou Diarra cancelled out Abdessamad Ezzalzouli's 35th-minute penalty in the 77th minute, leaves Mali unbeaten in their last three games.

Mali have never lost to Rwanda, winning three and drawing one of four World Cup qualifiers, with a 7-2 aggregate goal record.

The latest two meetings were a 1-0 home win on September 1, 2021 and a 3-0 win in Kigali on November 11, 2021, yet Da Silva has still described the chances of the two teams as equal.

The Amavubi began with a 3-1 win over Liberia in Kigali on September 25, with Abeddy Biramahire scoring in the second minute, Leroy Mickels in the 33rd and Joy-Lance Mickels from the penalty spot in the 44th.

In Praia on September 29 they trailed to Gilson Benchimol's 40th-minute goal, before Claude Niyomugabo equalised in first-half stoppage time with a long-range strike from a corner.

Elie Tatou Iradukunda scored the winner in the 52nd minute after a mistake by Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, and Rwanda were outshot 19-6 over the 90 minutes.

Stephen Constantine, in his second spell as Rwanda coach, declared after that win that "the revolution has begun", and his side also drew 0-0 with Kenya on October 5 in an international friendly match in Kigali.

Rwanda are chasing a first AFCON finals appearance since 2004, and Constantine has said he will take one game at a time while rating Group K as containing two of the better teams in Africa.

They have never beaten Mali, scoring only two goals in four meetings, and have conceded in both qualifiers so far.

Mali Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Rwanda Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Tia, who has scored twice in two caps for Mali, is out with an ankle injury, while Adama Camara (hamstring) and Lassana Coulibaly (biceps femoris) are also unavailable.

West Ham midfielder Mohamadou Kante receives his first call-up after choosing Mali over France and Senegal, and Swansea City winger Moussa Yeo, 22, is also new after scoring three times in his last five club games.

Gaoussou Diakite of Red Bull Salzburg and Fode Doucoure of Nantes return in a 24-man squad that does not include Yves Bissouma, who joined Ajax in late September, with no reason given for his absence.

For the visitors, Constantine trimmed his squad on Monday, November 9, dropping Elie Ganijuru, Kevin Muhire, Taiba Mbonyumwami and goalkeeper Yves Mugisha, while Fidele Uwiyaremye had already been sent home on the first day of camp for disciplinary reasons.

Defender Thierry Manzi and midfielder Jean Bosco Ruboneka are back after missing the September qualifiers, and Bonheur Mugisha, Gilbert Mugisha and Leroy-Jacques Mickels joined the camp on Monday.

Diarra; Traore, O Camara, Guindo, Gassama; Dieng, Sangare, K. Doumbia; Dorgeles, M. Doumbia, Sinayoko

Ntwari; Niyomugabo, Kavita, Mutsinzi, Byiringiro; Bizimana, B. Mugisha; L. Mickels, J. Mickels, G. Mugisha; Biramahire

Mali have not lost to Rwanda in four attempts, and the visitors have not scored against them in either of the last two meetings.

Rwanda's winner in Praia came from a goalkeeping error and they were outshot 19-6 there, while Mali have conceded only Cabral's goal in two games, so chances should be scarce for the Amavubi in Bamako.

Tia's absence removes the scorer of two of Mali's four goals, which is why a narrow margin looks more likely than a repeat of the 3-0 in Kigali in 2021.

Rwanda have scored more than Mali, and with the return leg in Kigali on November 17 a draw in Bamako would suit them.

#1856. England vs Croatia LIVE: Nations League latest score, match stream, goal updates

All eyes will be on Harry Kane tonight as England host Croatia in their penultimate Nations League game. The Three Lions skipper tonight makes history as the record appearance-maker for the men’s senior team, with his 126th cap. He overtakes Peter Shilton, whose final game for England came at the 1990 World Cup.

It is yet another staggering achievement for Kane, who has already shattered the goal record with 91 strikes to date, which is 38 more than previous holder Wayne Rooney. Kane also tonight leads his country out as captain for the 98th time, which is eight more than Billy Wright and Bobby Moore.

Kane paraded the Ballon d’Or trophy, won 17 days ago down the road at the London Palladium, ahead of kick-off, before full focus was on another win over Croatia as they look to hunt down Spain and top their Nations League group. Follow the game LIVE below with our dedicated match blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau at Wembley.

95min: Rogers blazes over, and there’s the whistle!

England win, Kane scores. Same ol’, same ol’.

90min: Burn twice goes close at corners, but Croatia do just enough to put him off.

86min: Garner thinks he has scored his first England goal, but Bellingham is offside in the build-up.

85min: Into the final five minutes. Croatia are not giving up.

More boos for Ben White as he enters the fray.

England’s support have not had an awful lot to get roused by tonight, but they let White know their feelings.

77min: Triple England change as White, Nguomha and Garner replace Gordon, Alexander-Arnold and Rice.

Modric is on for Croatia, replacing Misic.

70min: Kane is searching for goal no.93 and bullies Vuskovic something fierce by climbing all over him, and the referee blows up.

68min: It is another goal for Kane, but also another important one.

With Spain beating Czechia, England need to win tonight to stand any chance of topping the group come Sunday night.

Harry Kane makes a night all about himself, all about himself.

63min: Of course he does, straight down the middle. England lead!
